Prasa's Big rail blunder

By: Sian Clark | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa has committed the most expensive blunder in

Summary:
PRASA put out a tender for R600 million for 70 AFro 4000 locomotives to run on it's Shosholoza Meyl passenger line but the trains don't meet the country's rail height requirements. Apparently the 13 already delivered are too high for the route they are meant to be using. They exceed the height limit. The trains are currently being tested in Gauteng and Port Elizabeth but to get them there Transnet had to switch off the overhead cable lines to allow the trains to move. Prasa swears that the trains fulfil the rail safety requirements. Then there is also the other side of it. The unions are furious that the tenders were given to foreign companies who have BEE partners. They say that SA companies should be awarded. The company who got the job is also in question: In May this year workers went on strike against Nepotism and corruption within PRASA>

Further information:
PRASA have made two expensive blunders.
There are two tenders in question here: PRASA put out a tender for R60 million for 70 AFro 4000 locomotives to run on it's Shosholoza Meyl passenger line but the trains don't meet the country's rail height requirements. Apparently the 13 already delivered are too high for the route they are meant to be using. They exceed the height limit. The trains are currently being tested in Gauteng and Port Elizabeth but to get them there Transnet had to switch off the overhead cable lines to allow the trains to move. Prasa swears that the trains fulfil the rail safety requirements. The contract was awarded to a Spanish company.

The second tender R51 million tender for the wagons for these trains.
The contract was awarded to a French company with a local BEE partner. One of the stipulations is that they use local products. So there is Pressure put on local manufacturers of train components to supply this company with products at drastically reduced prices. The locals are saying they can't do it at such ridiculous prices. Prasa CEO has gone on record saying he has concerns about the French company's ability to keep to the contract's local content requirements.



Then there is also the other side of it. The unions are furious that the tenders were given to foreign companies who have BEE partners. They say that SA companies should be awarded. The company who got the job is also in question: In May this year workers went on strike against Nepotism and corruption within PRASA.

The companies involved have relations to Zuma Foundation and to ANC.

They have found that the chief engineer of PRASA is not registered as an engineer. he has been suspended. The CEO Lucky Montana has been fired as of 16th July. he was going to announce his

Press Release:


PRASA’S Big Blunder
A disgruntled board chairperson, an axed CEO, an unqualified engineer and trains that are too big for their tracks. Has the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA) finally derailed? What’s behind one of the country’s biggest tender debacles? Carte Blanche investigates the truth behind a R3.5 billion tender for 70 locomotives and the in-house battles for contracts at the agency.


Script:


CARTE BLANCHE PRASA
SCRIPTWRITER: SIAN CLARK
VOICEOVER: BONGANI BINGWA
VOICE: SATURDAY 1ST AUGUST 09H00

TX: 2ND AUGUST 2015

Last month the public were treated to a daily dose of the latest Soap opera to hit our shores - Prasa – The Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa.


It’s got all the essential elements for a potential blockbuster.

A disgruntled Minister, an axed CEO, a fake engineer and trains which are allegedly too big for the tracks.

Soundbite: Pieter-Louis Myburgh Investigative journalist
00.06.36 prasa has blatantly gone and by purchasing these afro 40000


Soundbite: Dinga Sikwebu, Numsa – I think that there is something rotten in the parastatal ..

The hero in this story is the Diesel Afro 4000, the new supposed prince of the South African rails.

It has speeds of up to 130Km per hour and will replace the Shosholozo Meyl passenger fleet which have served the country since 2006, transporting over 4 million passengers annually from all the major South African centres.

Bongani Link
00.02 our country railway infrastucture been in place for decades so when buy new modern loco .. no brainer …. except it appears we may have bought the wrong trains … 00.15

The new Afro 4000 locomotive imported from Spanish company Vossloh Espana is the first chapter in Prasa’s decade long fleet overhaul project.

The contract was signed in March 2013.




The contract is for:
20 Afro 4000 diesel locomotives and 50 diesel/electric locomotives.
The cost R3.5 billion rand.



Last month Rapport Newspaper’s investigative Journalist Pieter-Louis Myburgh revealed concerns that the trains exceeded the Maximum allowed height and possibly couldn’t run on some routes they were meant for.


Up sound: Pieter-Louis Meyburgh
UP SOUND: PIETER
00.03.35 the key concern here in terms of railway engineers is that the loco exceeds height restriction for a diesel locomotive….


The diesel Afro 4000 is 4140 mm
South African maximum height is 3965 mm

The diesel train is 175mm higher than regulation.

There is concern that this height increase places the top of the train too close to the powerlines.



Prasa CEO Lucky Montana vehemently denied to the press that there were problems with the height.


Upsound LIVE Lucky Montana
In our testing we have gone through not bridges but tunnels. 00.13.40


UP SOUND BONGANI


The PRASA report ends by suggesting the import be delayed.



Vossloh’s response indicated that the locomotive had been built to the specs provided by PRASA engineers and was acceptable for South African standards.
Carte Blanche asked Professor Edward Chikuni a Former South African Railway Electrical Engineer to comment.

UPSOUND EDWARD: 00.02.03 I don't think there is any threat to electrocution or flashovers … . . . .

Surprisingly Professor Chikuni stated that from the details of the report he did not deem it necessary to replace any overhead power lines and that the trains would pass safely through.


UP SOUND PROFESSOR
00.03.38 from an engineering point of view they are quite safe.

UPSOUND EDWARD: 00.09.34 this is the distance which is specified by the international organisations IT IS 150 mm from here to here.


But the release of the documents were damning so Prasa reacted by hosting a press conference.


UPSOUND FROM CONFERENCE.
I want to assure the country … govt I WANT TO SASURE THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH AFRICA public and the world that Prasa has bought the best possible trains. NOT ONLY IN OUR COUNTRY BUT IN THE WORLD

Dr Daniel Mtimkulu, was proudly introduced as the head of Engineering Services at Prasa.

UP SOUND DANIEL: WE’VE GOT TWO CRITICAL STANDARDS WHICH IS THE … ELECTFICAL SAFETFY INSTRUCTIONS AND SPECIFICATIONS.

3 days later Daniel Mthimkulu resigned when it was revealed he had not obtained an engineering degree or a doctorate as he claimed he had.

Carte Blanche determined he was registered as an Engineering Technologist and not qualified to run with huge technical projects.

Earlier this week Daniel Mtimkulu was charged with fraud.

BONGANI LINK:
00.01.48 it wasn’t just the height … that was in contention .. ISSUES COME TO THE FORE certainly what kicked the hornets nest ..


UP SOUND PETER
00.07.34 If you look at the tender documents … there are real concerns that key role players in this industry who were involved in this process who basically say that this been suggestion set up for vossloh espana to win it. …


These were obviously questions which Prasa needed to answer so we confirmed an interview time with Lucky Montana.

UP SOUND: HAVING AGREEED TO AN INTERVIEW …. BONGANI ON CELL PHONE BEEN ALL DAY AND CANCELLED … ALL I GET IS HIS VOICEMAIL.

Undettered Carte Blanche continued to proceed with interviews.

Spokesperson for Local Manufacturers Coenraad Bezuidenhout says the ruckus at Prasa has focused attention on preferential procurement.


UP SOUND: COENRAAD BEZUIDENHOUR 00.07.09 we have to approach govt to make sure locals manufacturers to actually get a slice of the action which IS FAIR AND allows them to scale up fair and to support the products they sell after the sales have already been made ….– we think we can do much better than overseas done in case of prasa. PROCUREMENT


DINGA SINGWE
00.01.20 many of the boards have been nonfunctional – THEY’VE BEEN there’s been a merry go round of executives


NUMSA’S Dinga Sikwebu is peeved that the lucrative Prasa contract was awarded to an overseas company.

UP SOUND: DINGA FROM NUMSA .. we as a country we just import everything. we are becoming a warehouse for all the things that are manufactured in other countries. deceimates job …. dead cities.


UP SOUND PRESS CONFERENCE: LUCKY MONTANA THE UNIONS ARE ASKING ME TO BUY FORM HERE. THE LOCOMOTIVES WE BOUGHT COULD NOT HAVE BEEN BOUGHT BUILT BY ANY COMPANHY HERE.


The handling of hedging is the latest question raised over the tender. Reports show that inadequate foreign currency hedging in this contract could force PRASA to end up paying almost 5 BILLION RAND instead of the contracted 3.5bILLION RAND.

Up sound: DINGA 00.14.16 one of the things you factor is that by the time the product is delivered the value of the rand will have changed.

00.15.16 00.15.16 the fact that this ALLEGED CLAIMED doesn’t happen is a sign that you had a procurement system that is quite sick.

The next shock installment in the Prasa saga soon followed.
CEO Lucky Montana was fired.
UP SOUND: I HAVE NO DOUBT …. IT’S UNLAWFUL AND NEVER ACCEPT IT.


BONGANI
file: 012
At heart of relationship breakdown between Montana AND THE the board is the issue of payment to supplier supposedly connected to governing party …. ALLEGED several emails and sms from minister urging to make the payment. governing party … he maintains this was interference. 00.01.



UP SOUND LUCKY ON RADIO:
00.28 … For a period of almost 8 months we been having running battles with the board … with the Chairman of Board. 00.06.45 He is going to lose the war. He is also going to lose the moral fight. He knows that it was a cowardly decision.


So with the CEO fired Carte Blanche confirmed an interview with the Prasa Chairman Popo Molefe.

UP SOUND: POPO
BONGANI link
COMING OUT OF PRASA
00.02.16 we had a scheduled interview pop molefe minister instructed not engage on any matters.

It’s been a comedy of errors at the expense of the taxpayer. Dramatic true-life daily episodes have amused and astonished the public for the past month. It’s been four weeks Prasa would like to forget, but it seems it’s not likely to go away quietly.

Lucky Montana is making sure his grievances are heard. On Thursday, the axed former CEO laid fraud and criminal charges against Prasa members.

UP SOUND: DINGA 00.15.31 I think that we as tax payers and passengers will have to pay for what is a silly blunder
LUCKY MONTANA
There is no story.


ENDS ENDS ENDS

Prasa swears that the trains fulfil the rail safety requirements. The contract was awarded to a Spanish company. The second tender R51 million tender for the wagons for these trains. The contract was awarded to a French company with a local BEE partner. One of the stipulations is that they use local products. So there is Pressure put on local manufacturers of train components to supply this company with products at drastically reduced prices.
